newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB down after Murdoch comments.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB down after Murdoch comments.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc fell in early trade on Monday after a weekend report said Rupert Murdoch, chairman of News Corp -- which owns 40 percent of Sky shares -- described the stock as "overpriced."
The stock was down 11-1/2p at 432-1/2 by 0715 GMT in volume of 30,000 shares.
The Sunday Times, owned by Murdoch's News Corp, quoted Murdoch as saying he could not understand the fuss over a recent decline in BSkyB shares. "BSkyB was grossly overpriced."
The paper pointed out that even after falling sharply in recent weeks, BSkyB was still one of London's most highly rated companies, trading on a historic multimple of 32.6 times earnings.

The rout in the stock was propelled by the announcement of the departure of chief executive Sam Chisolm and deputy managing director David Chance. The company was also excluded from a group bidding for a digital TV licence.
